rationale: C17 is a highly plausible drafting template. Both are presidential reply letters concerning a named Catholic cardinal persecuted by a Communist government, and both move from acknowledging the correspondent's message, to condemning Communist repression of religion, to asserting that coercion cannot extinguish religious faith or spirit. The child adapts C17's concrete rhetorical and structural machinery from Cardinal Wyszynski in Poland to Cardinal Mindszenty in Hungary. C10 has related language about Communist repression of religious life and the sympathy of the free world, but its anniversary-message structure is less closely parallel. C04 shares the theme of spiritual resistance to Communist oppression, but not the distinctive cardinal-and-religious-liberty letter framework.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I have your telegram of January twenty-third on behalf of the United Catholic Organizations for the Freeing of Cardinal Mindszenty.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I have your letter of October fourteenth regarding the action taken recently against a courageous leader of his Church, Stefan Cardinal Wyszynski, Primate of Poland.
shared_material.explanation: Both open by acknowledging a dated communication concerning Communist action against a specifically named Catholic cardinal.

shared_material.child_excerpt: They regarded the attack upon him as a blow against religious freedom in Hungary and an unprincipled attempt to destroy spiritual and moral influences in that country.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The calculated repression of all religious organization in the Communist States makes it apparent that wherever Communists are in position to use force and violence, they will do so in an effort to win domination not only over the body and mind of man, but over his soul as well.
shared_material.explanation: Both characterize persecution of the cardinal as part of a calculated Communist assault upon religion and spiritual life.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Communist assault upon religious liberty and leadership in Hungary has failed, however, to turn the Hungarian people from their faith in God.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the religious spirit of man will never be subdued or extinguished, and that it will remain a sustaining force Poland during the present tragic suffering of the Polish people.
shared_material.explanation: The central reassurance is materially parallel: Communist coercion cannot extinguish religious faith, which persists among the afflicted nation's people.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Despite the constraints of person and silence imposed on Cardinal Mindszenty and other church leaders by their persecutors, the spirit of these men has defied confinement by the totalitarian State.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Communist violations of the inalienable rights of man under God do not go unopposed, and that they are effectively exposed in every forum.
shared_material.explanation: Both conclude by contrasting Communist confinement or violations with the enduring force of religious conviction and opposition from the free world.
